predecessors.name: Northern Wei
predecessors.text: Gao Huan's Eastern Wei: Hebei, Shandong, eastern Shanxi and Henan, the Cliopatria 534 shape

successors.name: Northern Qi
successors.text: the Eastern Wei realm at its end, the Cliopatria 546 shape

ledger.x: 534: the capital moves from Luoyang to Yecheng.
534: Gao Huan sets up Yuan Shanjian as emperor of the Eastern Wei.
537: the Eastern and Western Wei fight over western Henan and southwestern Shanxi.
537: the Western Wei take western Henan and southwestern Shanxi.
538: the Luoyang siege ends with the Western Wei gone.
543: Gao Zhongmi hands Hulao to the Western Wei.
543: the Western Wei are driven off.
547: Hou Jing takes the Henan provinces out of the Eastern Wei.
549: the Liang provinces north of the Yangtze submit to the Eastern Wei.
550: Gao Yang deposes Yuan Shanjian and founds the Northern Qi.

wars.name: Eastern Wei-Western Wei wars
wars.outcome: Gao Huan's incursion of spring 536 (Xia Province), his defeat at Shayuan in winter 537, the siege of Luoyang in fall 538, Hulao in spring 543 and the 50-day siege of Yubi in fall 546 (Wei Xiaokuan held) leave the Luoyang region Eastern Wei and western Henan…

wars.name: Hou Jing's defection and rebellion in Henan
wars.outcome: Hou Jing offers the 13 provinces he commanded to the Western Wei and Liang in spring 547; the Eastern Wei put the rebellion down and Hou flees to Shouyang.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line on the pages.
